findings.title: The sidecar save panels and Export Scientific Bundle can replace the source dataset (CR3's refusal only covers Preprocess and Export Data…)
findings.failure_scenario: The dataset scan.h5 is open. The user gets the 'Choose Session Sidecar' panel, either on a first Save Calibration/Save to Results or from Dataset > Change Session Sidecar…. The panel opens in the dataset's folder, next to scan.h5, and the sidecar error text tells the user to 'choose that file'. The user clicks scan.h5 by mistake and confirms Replace. (1) First-save path: mergeCalibration/mergeResultMap builds a new sidecar and rename(2)s it over scan.h5. The raw 4D cube becomes a ~10 kB session file. (2) Change… path: copySidecarFile runs removeItem(scan.h5) and then copyItem. If the copy fails (for example the current sidecar is unreadable because of EPERM, the exact state this remedy is offered for), nothing replaces the deleted dataset. Either way the bookmark is then remembered with the dataset path as its own sidecar. Export Scientific Bundle… has the same gap: choosing scan.h5 renames the bundle over the source. The 2026-10-02 Export Data… guard was never applied here.
findings.evidence: ResultExport.swift:1027 `guard panel.runModal() == .OK, let url = panel.url else { return nil }` then `:1028 _ = url.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource(); return url`, with no exportDestinationRefusal. :152-160 writableSessionSidecarURL adopts it. :369-373 exportScientificBundle `panel.runModal() == .OK, let url = panel.url` goes straight to writeScientificBundle (compare ProductDataExport.swift:44 `if let line = BraggVectorEMDWriter.exportDestinationRefusal(url, ...)`). SessionSidecarLocator.swift:420-424 `if manager.fileExists(atPath: url.path) { try manager.removeItem(at: url) ... } try manager.copyItem(at: current, to: url)`. grep shows exportDestinationRefusal is called only from PreprocessExport.swift:113, ProductDataExport.swift:44 and the writer itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse the source file in runSidecarSavePanel (both sidecar paths) and in exportScientificBundle with BraggVectorEMDWriter.exportDestinationRefusal / isSameFile against descriptor.filePath, before any write. In copySidecarFile, copy to a temporary file on the same volume and rename it over the destination (or use replaceItemAt), so the destination is never removed before the copy exists.

(1) First save: ResultExport.swift:147-162 writableSessionSidecarURL → runSidecarSavePanel (:1020-1030: NSSavePanel, directoryURL = dataset folder, no refusal, returns any URL with scope started) → sessionSidecar.adopt → saveCalibrationToSessionSidecar (:1218-1225) → BraggVectorEMDWriter.mergeCalibration (:476-477 `existing = fileExists ? destination : nil`) → publish → writeFile opens scan.h5 read-only (:1802-1807; it IS HDF5 so this succeeds, but it has no session root so nothing is preserved) → Darwin.rename(temporary, destination) at :1386-1392 unconditionally. The dataset path now holds a session file; the open inode survives only until the dataset is closed. The grant is then remembered against the dataset path (rememberSidecarGrant :1234). (2) Change…: saveSessionSidecarAs (:1077-1094) → the same panel → adoptSessionSidecar → SessionSidecarLocator.copySidecarFile (:400-435): the only guards are current==url and current-vs-url file identity; then `removeItem(url)` BEFORE `copyItem` — the code's own failure text admits it ("was removed before the copy failed", :429-431). findings.title: The sidecar path is derived from the file stem only, so scan.dm4 and scan.h5 in one folder share one session file, and nothing in the sidecar says which source it belongs to
findings.failure_scenario: A common py4DSTEM layout: scan.dm4 (raw) and scan.h5 (the py4DSTEM-converted copy, often bin_Q(2)) in the same folder. Both map to scan.mac4dstem.h5. Opening scan.h5 restores scan.dm4's session. applySessionCalibration adopts its Q pixel size and origin because both views are 'full extent' (no detector-shape check), so a 2x-binned h5 gets a Q scale off by 2x and an origin in the other detector's pixels. Its saved results and recipe are adopted as this file's. Any save from either file then rewrites the shared sidecar's calibration, replay record, lineage and labels with that file's values, destroying the other dataset's session. In the sandboxed app this is reached through Allow Access… (which accepts the file because it IS the derived sibling) or through the first-save panel's Replace.
findings.evidence: BraggVectorEMDWriter.swift:202-207 `let stem = source.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent; return source.deletingLastPathComponent().appendingPathComponent(stem + SessionSidecarFormat.nameSuffix ...)` (nameSuffix ".mac4dstem.h5", HDF5Types.swift:28). writeFile (:1812-1820) writes no source path or identity, and loadSession (:555-685) checks none. Only the labels are path-checked (DiskCentreLabels.swift:345 `guard decoded.filePath == filePath`), and their own error text says they 'belong to scan.dm4'. AppState+Open.swift:1038-1050 adopts the calibration by view policy alone.
findings.suggested_fix: Include the source extension in the sidecar name for new sessions (scan.dm4.mac4dstem.h5, with a read-fallback for the old name). Also record the source file name and shape on the sidecar root, and refuse to restore or rewrite a sidecar whose recorded source is a different file.

On restore nothing identifies the source: loadSession (:555-690) reads calibration, results, specification, replay, lineage — no source name, no native shape, no throw on a mismatch; SessionSidecarSnapshot (BraggVectorEMDTypes.swift:175-194) carries none. AppState+Open.swift:1028-1050 → SessionCalibrationFramePolicy.decide(.recorded(.fullExtent), loaded: .fullExtent) → `session == loaded` → .identity → adopted verbatim (Q pixel size and origin in the OTHER detector's pixels; off by the bin_Q factor). The only shape gate anywhere is AppState.swift:1309-1317 `.doesNotFit`, which fires only when a recorded CROP cannot build a LoadView — `.fullExtent` (LoadSpecification.swift:91, no dims) always builds. Only labels are path-checked (DiskCentreLabels.swift:345-347). Sandbox: Allow Access… (:1057) accepts the file because isSameFile(url, expected) compares against the same stem-derived path. Every writer entry point rebuilds the whole file (writeFile), so a save from either dataset replaces the other's calibration/recipe/lineage/labels. The writer already has an unused `source_file` key (BraggVectorEMDTypes.swift:332) and writes Rshape/Qshape only inside the BraggVectors node (:2396-2398).
verify.test_hint: (1) `XCTAssertNotEqual(BraggVectorEMDWriter.sessionSidecarURL(forSourcePath: "/d/scan.dm4"), sessionSidecarURL(forSourcePath: "/d/scan.h5"))` — red today. (2) Writer round trip: mergeCalibration(qWidth: 256, qHeight: 256, to: sidecar) with source name "scan.dm4"; then loadSession for a dataset whose native shape is 128×128 / name scan.h5 must report a source mismatch (snapshot.calibration not adoptable / throws) — red today because the snapshot carries no identity and the policy returns .identity.
verify.fix_sketch: Record on the session root at every write: source file name and native (ry, rx, qy, qx) — the file's shape, not the loaded view's, so a crop/bin reopen of the same file still matches. On load, a mismatch becomes a `.doesNotFit`-class refusal (which also arms sidecarRewriteRefusal, so no save can clobber the other dataset's session). Naming (scan.dm4.mac4dstem.h5 for new sessions with a read-fallback to the stem name) is the owner's call — his existing sidecars are under the old name. The restore is refused: 'The saved disk-centre labels was labelled in the native frame … — not applied', or 'the sidecar's disk-centre labels belong to …'. findings.title: A sidecar that exists but cannot be opened at write time is treated as absent, and a fresh file is renamed over it
findings.failure_scenario: The dataset opens with its session restored. The user then inspects scan.mac4dstem.h5 in HDFView (whose default Open is read/write) or in h5py with mode 'r+'/'a'. The bundled HDF5 2.1.1 locks files by default, so the app's read-only H5Fopen of the existing sidecar fails. writeFile turns that into existingID = nil. The save writes a new file holding only the current calibration (plus the one map being saved) and rename(2)s it over the sidecar. Every saved result, the stored BraggVectors, the labels, the recipe and the lineage are gone with no error. A sidecar truncated after open behaves the same way. The rewrite gate only covers failures at open time.
findings.evidence: BraggVectorEMDWriter.swift:1802-1807 `let existingID: hid_t? = existing.flatMap { source in let id = ... h5.h5fopen($0, h5FileReadOnly, h5DefaultProperty); return id >= 0 ? id : nil }`. `existing` is non-nil only when the file exists (:408-409, :442-443, :476-477 `FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: destination.path) ? destination : nil`). Publish then renames unconditionally (:1386-1392). No H5Pset_file_locking or HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING anywhere in mac4DSTEM/ or tools/; `strings libhdf5.dylib` reports 'HDF5 library version: 2.1.1'.
findings.suggested_fix: When `existing` is non-nil and H5Fopen fails, throw the HDF5 error (hdf5Failure("opening the existing session sidecar")) instead of continuing as if no file were there. Apply the same refusal when the file opens but has no session root, unless the caller is a first save that the user explicitly confirmed.

verify.reason: BraggVectorEMDWriter.swift:1802-1807: `existingID = existing.flatMap { id = h5fopen(path, readOnly, default); return id >= 0 ? id : nil }` — every open failure on a file that fileExists (:408-409, :442-443, :476-477) collapses to "no existing file". Every preservation branch (existingResults :1831+, BraggVectors copy, replay/lineage, labels :1891) is gated on `existingID`, so the temporary holds only the current calibration (+ the one map), and publish renames it over the sidecar unconditionally (:1386-1392) — no error, no status. The locking trigger holds: the bundled ./libhdf5.dylib reports "HDF5 library version: 2.1.1" and contains "Unable to lock file" (locking compiled in; default on since 1.10 — a RDWR open elsewhere takes LOCK_EX, a RDONLY H5Fopen then fails); grep finds no H5Pset_file_locking / HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING in mac4DSTEM/, tools/ or tests, and every h5fopen passes h5DefaultProperty. The stronger variant is independent of locking: any unopenable sidecar (truncated, bad superblock, unreadable permissions with a writable folder) is silently replaced. sidecarRewriteRefusal (SessionGates.swift:187) only reflects failures recorded at open time, so a sidecar that restored fine and then became unopenable passes the gate. Re-rated high: silent loss of every saved result, vectors, labels, recipe and lineage; medium only if the owner judges the concurrent-r/w-reader precondition rare. Note SessionLineageSidecarTests.swift:359 pins that an unreadable lineage ATTRIBUTE does not block a save — that is a different case (file opens, one attribute fails) and must stay green.
verify.test_hint: Write a sidecar with one result + labels via mergeResultMap; truncate the file to 200 bytes (or write 200 random bytes under the same name so H5Fopen fails while fileExists is true); call mergeCalibration(..., to: sidecar). Assert it throws WriterError.hdf5("opening the existing session sidecar") and the file's bytes are unchanged. Red today: the call succeeds and loadInventory then reports a fresh sidecar with no results.

findings.title: A binned view sizes streaming tiles by post-bin bytes but every reader allocates the pre-bin tile: bin² (4x/16x/64x) blow-up of the 'bounded' transient
findings.failure_scenario: On an 8 GB Mac, open a 256x256 scan x 256x256 detector DM4 (uint16, 8.6 GB file) in the configurator and pick bin 4x (the refusal text itself says 'Crop or bin to enable'). scanTileRows budgets min(GPU/8, physical/24) = 358 MB of POST-bin rows: 358 MB / (256*64*64*4 = 4.2 MB) = 85 rows. DM4Reader.readScanTile (rowsAreContiguous: no detector crop, full width) then decodes 85*256*65536 floats = 5.7 GB of anonymous [Float] before view.binned() reduces it, plus the binned copy and the prefetched tile, during the opening virtual-image pass and every later tiled pass (mean/max pattern, origins, Detect All, keep-in-memory fill). At bin 8x the rows cap at the whole scan: a 17 GB transient on an 8 GB Mac. On the owner's 64 GB Mac, the 28.5 GB 060 DM4 at bin 4 runs as one 330-row tile: a 28.5 GB anonymous buffer next to the 28.5 GB mapped file, per pass. This is the swap-exhaustion class of the 2026-09-24 kernel panic, on a path that claims to stream. H5Reader has the same shape (hyperslab read at pre-bin extent). The 28 GB parity run did not cover it: that probe read pattern-by-pattern, not readScanTile.
findings.evidence: FourDArray.swift:367-368 `let bytesPerRow = descriptor.rx * descriptor.qy * descriptor.qx * MemoryLayout<Float>.stride` (descriptor = view, post-bin); :397 `let hostBudget = max(1, Int(ProcessInfo.processInfo.physicalMemory) / 24)`; :399 `let budgetRows = max(1, budget / max(1, bytesPerRow))`. DM4Reader.swift:381-382 `let raw = try decode(byteOffset: start, count: range.count * rowPix)` / `pixels = view.binned(raw, patternCount: range.count * rx)` with rowPix = rx*qy*qx at SOURCE detector size; DM4Reader.swift:422-423 `var out = [Float](repeating: 0, count: count)`. H5Reader.swift:720-721 `let pixelCount = slab.count.reduce(1) { $0 * Int($1) }` / `var buffer = [Float](repeating: 0, count: pixelCount)` (slab count = pre-bin read crop), then :730 `view.binned(buffer, ...)`. LoadSpecification.swift:89 `availableBinFactors = [2, 4, 8]`. No detectorBin term anywhere in scanTileRows.
findings.suggested_fix: Size the tile from the bytes the reader actually allocates: in scanTileRows use the read extent (view.readDetectorCrop ?? source qy/qx) instead of the post-bin descriptor, i.e. divide budgetRows by detectorBin² (pure refusal/tiling arithmetic; tile size changes float grouping of the cross-tile reducers only for binned views, so it needs a parity re-run). Alternatively bin inside the readers row-by-row or pattern-by-pattern so the pre-bin buffer stays one row. Fixture: a binned synthetic cube with maximumRows nil asserting peak allocated floats <= budget.

verify.reason: Weaker variant than reported. Traced: FourDArray.swift:367-399 sizes rows from the POST-bin descriptor (descriptor = view.descriptor, FourDArray.swift:39; LoadSpecification.swift:317-330 derives it from the binned extent) with no detectorBin term; H5Reader.swift:720-730 `read()` allocates `pixelCount` = product of slab.count, which hyperslab() builds at the READ (pre-bin) detector extent over the whole tile's scan rows, then bins afterwards — so an H5 tile of N post-bin rows allocates bin² times the budget (8 GB Mac, 256²×256² uint16 at bin 4: 341 MB budget → 85 rows → 5.5 GB pre-bin [Float]; at bin 8 the rows cap at ry and the pre-bin buffer is the whole 17 GB cube). DM4 scan-fastest has the same shape: scanFastestGather (DM4Reader.swift:209-235) allocates `count * height * width` at readDetectorCrop extent for the whole tile. BUT the reviewer's headline DM4 scenario is wrong: LoadSpecification.swift:317 sets readDetectorCrop NON-nil whenever bin > 1, so rowsAreContiguous(view) (DM4Reader.swift:308-313) is false for every binned view and the detector-fastest DM4 reader takes the per-row → per-pattern path (DM4Reader.swift:162-183), decoding one pre-bin pattern at a time into a post-bin tile buffer (reserveCapacity at view extent, :395-398). findings.failure_scenario: Parallax products go stale by being cleared: every calibration setter does `phaseContrast.parallaxPreprocess = nil; parallaxAlignment = nil`, and there is no staleness key. 1. Start Parallax preprocessing, which can take minutes on a large cube. The R pixel size, voltage and origin are captured into `physical` at :45. 2. While it runs, type a corrected R pixel size or voltage in Prepare. These fields are not disabled while busy, and the edit does not cancel the operation. The setter clears the (still nil) preprocess. 3. The run finishes; its guard checks only the token and the epoch, so `phaseContrast.parallaxPreprocess = result` installs a preprocess built with the old wavelength and scan sampling. It is shown as 'Parallax preprocessing ✓'. Alignment, the aberration fit (C1 in Å) and depth sectioning then run from it, and the exported sampling is the old value. Alignment (:160) has the same gap: an edit mid-alignment clears both products, then the alignment lands with parallaxPreprocess still nil.
findings.evidence: AppState+PhaseContrast.swift:45 `physical = try ParallaxPhysicalCalibration.resolve(calibration: calibrationSession.calibration, ...)`; :77-79 `guard isCurrentOperation(token), datasetSession.epoch == epoch, !token.isCancelled else { return }` / `phaseContrast.parallaxPreprocess = result`; :158-160 the same for alignment. AppState+Open.swift:1393-1397 `func setManualRPixelSize` ... `phaseContrast.parallaxPreprocess = nil`; :1424-1426 setManualAcceleratingVoltage does the same. CalibrationReadinessRow.swift:219/:245 and PrepareSettings.swift:167: the fields have no `.disabled(appState.isBusy)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a calibration-revision counter to PhaseContrastProduct and bump it wherever the products are cleared. Capture it at run start and refuse to land (with a status line) when it changed, or compare the result's `calibration` against a fresh `ParallaxPhysicalCalibration.resolve` before installing it. For alignment, also require `phaseContrast.parallaxPreprocess` to be the same instance it started from.

verify.reason: The precondition 'the fields are not disabled while busy' is false. PrepareSettings.body (UI/PrepareSettings.swift:142-227) wraps the whole settings Group — PatternStatisticsSection, the Calibration section with every readinessRow (:155, which renders CalibrationReadinessRow.manualScale incl. the R field at UI/CalibrationReadinessRow.swift:239-247), the voltage OptionalNumericField (:161-168), diagnosticsSection and ellipseCorrectionSection — in `.disabledWhileRunning(appState)` at UI/PrepareSettings.swift:227, which is `disabled(appState.isBusy)` (UI/LayoutPolicy.swift:523-525). prepareParallaxPreview and alignment both run under beginCancellableOperation (App/AppState+PhaseContrast.swift:56, :133) → OperationCenter.begin sets isBusy = true (Session/OperationCenter.swift:104-106) until finish. setManualRPixelSize / setManualRPixelUnits / setManualAcceleratingVoltage have no other UI callers (grep over UI/ and App/: only CalibrationReadinessRow.swift:219/231/245 and PrepareSettings.swift:167). The reviewer looked for .disabled on the individual fields and missed the enclosing group modifier. The landing guards (:77-79, :158-160) are as described, but the edit that would make them insufficient cannot be committed while the run is busy.
verify.fix_sketch: None required. If a belt is wanted, compare result.calibration against a fresh ParallaxPhysicalCalibration.resolve before installing, but no live path reaches the gap.
